embeddedReportPolicy: Original reports are embedded in full, without rewriting their findings or provenance. Original session-path references identify historical inputs; embeddedReports resolves report references durably.

review.task: Independent initial full-task review of C1 animals/documents for stop-cran/learning-japanese#56
review.modelIdentityLimitation: The actual model/version was not exposed in this review's available context. No model identity has been inferred from branding or available-tool model lists.
review.summary: All 28 records were inspected. Three actionable findings concern a missing accepted 六匹 reading, rejected ordinary email counters, and Japanese questions that do not actually require the intended complete-document unit. Two narrower acceptance questions remain UNVERIFIED rather than being asserted incorrect or clean.

severityConvention.major: A visible task can penalize an ordinary interpretation or fail its intended distinction.
severityConvention.minor: A localized accepted-answer omission or a narrower consequential acceptance question.

snapshot.commitLimitation: The packet supplies a contentVersion and exact file hashes, not a Git commit or working-tree status. This review identifies only that frozen packet.
snapshot.snapshotHashInterpretation: The nine snapshot hashes match the frozen files' raw bytes. Do not silently substitute LF-normalized hashes; several files have CRLF.

article.scope: 頭, 羽, 部, 通 paragraphs and their corresponding reference bullets only
article.otherArticleText: Visible surrounding article text was treated only as context, not as additional review targets.

fieldsInspected: Every complete v1 Japanese question and noun
Every answer-side English translation and note, without using either to disambiguate the question
Every canonical phrase, reading, and readingAnswers entry
Every good, kana, and hard alternative; the 12 target forwards have no hard arrays
Every wrong option in its completed Japanese sentence
Both reverse option sets using actual displayed nouns and source-wide readings
All four complete external reverse dependency records, including the pen record's two hard branches
All v2 complete cues, written forms, writtenAnswers, readings, readingAnswers, and explanations
The indicated article paragraphs and reference identities
Operation-level row coverage and the independent five-component rubric
notPerformed: No other n3-implementation reports, agents, history, or live worktrees inspected
No builds, tests of application runtime, emulator, signing, commits, publishing, or content edits

runtimeInterpretation: V1 en and note are answer-side.
V1 alternative-unit kana belongs in suffix typing, not necessarily canonical Read.
Kana that already normalizes to a good entry is not assumed rejected; this includes セット and ワンセット spellings.
Every canonical Read list remains specific to its displayed unit.
V2 supplied-unit English cues earn Write/Read form-practice coverage only.
Existing dependency cards were not treated as targets for unrelated repairs.
N3 is an editorial study allocation, not an official vocabulary or counter inventory.

rubric.scale: 0, 1, 2 are the indices of the three descriptions in the supplied contract.
feedback: names form/result or no own reverse note
rubric.interpretation: Feedback increases with explanatory completeness, not difficulty. These are editorial vectors, not empirical difficulty scores. The calculation score is zero when the requested number is already supplied, including bu-expression-1. A provisional score is explicitly identified where acceptance is unresolved.

fileVerdicts.notes: All three forwards and the reverse remain present. Canonical 頭 readings, large/working-animal overlap, and noun distractors are sound; the accepted 六匹 alternate lacks one supported typed pronunciation.
Ten, eleven, and the interrogative are supplied-unit form practice; none is independent selection evidence.

The listed canonical 羽 pronunciations are supported. Six-animal alternate typing has the same omission as 頭. Whole-roast 羽 is verified, but the ordinary collocational status of its accepted 匹 alternative is not established by the retrieved entries.
The exact 8/10/11/question pronunciations are corroborated. The explicit unit requests legitimately exclude other counters in Write.

Copy/sheet and copy/volume overlap are correctly explained. The loose-handout question does not require copying all three sheets before the learner answers; its intended sheet-versus-complete-copy selection contrast is therefore not secure.
No contraction in 十部 or the 一部 component of 十一部. The 30-sheet observation is explanatory, not required arithmetic. Application-copy wording here does not add Japanese selection coverage.

The sealed letter and reverse are well differentiated. Email typing omits ordinary generic counters. The application question does not say both sheets were submitted. The ordinary stored-email collocation with 本 also needs more precise support.
All authored canonical readings are supported. Whether 八通 must reject はちつう remains unresolved; a table listing only はっつう does not prove exclusivity.

Accurate qualified descriptions, useful readings and state/unit contrasts. The 八通 example gives a supported default without explicitly asserting that no other pronunciation exists. The 部 source is correctly identified as Seisenban's ぶ entry, not Daijisen's historical べ entry. No official N3 allocation is claimed.

itemInventory.question: 牧場で牛を一{}見ました。
itemInventory.englishAssessment: Accurate: seeing one cow on a farm; no hidden question constraint.
itemInventory.assessment: Both animal units fit. All three wrong units fail the ordinary cow sense. The note properly separates canonical 一頭 from 一匹 pronunciation.

itemInventory.question: この動物園には、象が六{}います。
itemInventory.assessment: The canonical reading and all wrong choices are sound. ロクヒキ is an explicitly supported alternative reading of accepted 六匹 and is omitted from suffix typing, not from canonical Read.

itemInventory.question: この施設では、盲導犬が八{}訓練を受けています。
itemInventory.englishAssessment: Accurate; guide-dog training is not a training-session count.
itemInventory.assessment: Working-animal use and 頭/匹 overlap are supported. Both whole 頭 readings and both listed 匹 readings fit. Facility/guide dog/training vocabulary is supported.
牛 is uniquely ordinary with 頭. Notebook, pen, and car senses do not compete. No animal distractor or hidden forward-sentence limitation is needed. No independent reverse note is authored.

itemInventory.question: とじていない三枚一組の資料を、一{}コピーしてください。
itemInventory.englishAssessment: The English adds 'one complete copy' and 'count complete copies, not individual sheets'; these are not available to the learner before answering.
itemInventory.assessment: 部 and complete-set alternatives fit the intended all-pages interpretation; 組み is a recognized spelling and 一式 is いっしき, not the unrelated いちしき label. Loose pages exclude the ordinary bound-book 冊 interpretation; 台 fails. But 一枚コピー can request one sheet of the described loose material. The Japanese must specify copying the complete set if 枚 is to be wrong.

itemInventory.question: この一枚の申込書を、八{}コピーします。
itemInventory.englishAssessment: Accurate eight-copy statement; the single-sheet fact is explicitly Japanese-side.
itemInventory.assessment: Both unit choices count the same requested copies here. No contraction in はちぶ. Wrong animal/machine/cup units do not fit. The explanation does not generalize one-sheet equivalence to all documents.

itemInventory.question: 同じ本を六{}注文しました。
itemInventory.englishAssessment: The English's ordinary bound-book reading is compatible with 本, and 同じ is already visible.
itemInventory.assessment: Same-publication 部 and physical-book 冊 both fit. ろくぶ and ろくさつ are correct. None of the three wrong units is an ordinary count of these books. The modern ぶ suffix source, not historical べ, supports the distinction.

itemInventory.cue: There are ten cattle. Give the complete count using 頭, not a different animal counter.
itemInventory.assessment: Exact 10 readings verified; explanation correctly contrasts contracted ten with uncontracted 六頭. Unit supplied, no independent selection credit.

itemInventory.cue: Eleven guide dogs work at a training centre. Write their complete count using 頭.
itemInventory.assessment: Exact eleven reading verified. Final 一頭 contraction is explained. Dog-versus-session reminder is understandable but not a new independent context or operation.

itemInventory.cue: Ask how many cattle there are. Write only the question quantity using 何 and 頭.
itemInventory.assessment: The cue requests the quantity, not a whole question. なんとう is supported; the counter/noun distinction from 頭あたま is appropriate.

itemInventory.question: 庭でスズメが三{}えさを食べています。
itemInventory.assessment: Both listed 羽 readings and 三匹 reading are correct. General animal acceptance is not treated as a strict size rule. Wrong units fail. スズメ and えさ are kana-accessible but not glossed; see optional O1.

itemInventory.question: 農場で鶏を六{}飼っています。
itemInventory.englishAssessment: Accurate; 飼っています establishes live kept birds before answering.
itemInventory.assessment: Both canonical readings are directly supported; 六匹 acceptance again omits ろくひき. All wrong choices fail for the birds, not the farm buildings or eggs.

itemInventory.rubricQualification: The alternative-handling score is not a claim that every accepted collocation has been independently attested; 匹 remains U1.
itemInventory.question: 丸ごとのローストチキンを一{}注文しました。
itemInventory.englishAssessment: Accurate; whole rather than cut is already explicit in Japanese.
itemInventory.assessment: Whole cooked bird with 羽 is explicitly supported. General individual food-item counts 個/つ are coherent, and the supplied readings are correct. The exact cooked-chicken use of 匹 is less securely supported than live-animal usage. Wrong book/machine/cup units do not fit.

itemInventory.cue: Eight chickens are in a pen. Write the count using 羽.
itemInventory.assessment: Both exact eight readings supported. Explanatory はね distinction is correct; no unsupported rejection of the less common はっぱ.

itemInventory.cue: You can see ten birds in a garden. Write the count using 羽.
itemInventory.assessment: All three exact readings are directly discussed by Tofugu. IMABI's shorter row does not invalidate the other two. Contraction is not mandatory.

itemInventory.cue: Eleven chickens are in a pen. Write the complete count using 羽.
itemInventory.assessment: Exact eleven table entry confirms the final いちわ. This number swap extends form practice, not transfer-context coverage.

itemInventory.cue: Ask how many birds are in the garden. Write only the question quantity using 何 and 羽.
itemInventory.assessment: Both interrogative readings supported. The cue does not require a complete Japanese interrogative sentence.

itemInventory.cue: A loose handout contains three sheets per complete copy. Write the count for ten complete copies using 部, not the sheet total.
itemInventory.assessment: The number ten is supplied, so no multiplication is needed to answer. Thirty sheets in the explanation is correct and distinguishes the units. じゅうぶ is supported; じゅっぷ is not its reading.

itemInventory.cue: Eleven copies of the same book were ordered. Write the complete-copy count using 部, not 冊.
itemInventory.assessment: Regular full eleven reading retains いちぶ. The note explicitly recognizes 冊 as valid in ordinary book counting while distinguishing this supplied-form drill.

itemInventory.cue: Ask how many complete copies of an application form are required. Write only the question quantity using 何 and 部.
itemInventory.assessment: The interrogative and whole-copy explanation are correct. It is an English supplied-unit form task, not Japanese application-document unit selection.

itemInventory.question: 三枚の便箋に書いた手紙を封筒に入れ、のりで閉じて、一{}送りました。
itemInventory.englishAssessment: Accurate multi-sheet letter, envelope, sealing, and sending sequence.
itemInventory.assessment: The letter-entry evidence explicitly supports 通, correspondence 本, and sealed-letter 封 with these one-count readings. Three sheets enclosed as the letter distinguish its complete communication count from one sheet. Literary 葉/札 listings were not converted into unrestricted ordinary alternatives. Wrong animal and cup units fail.

itemInventory.question: まだ読んでいないメールが六{}あります。
itemInventory.englishAssessment: Accurate unread-message existence statement; no formal-register restriction is visible.
itemInventory.assessment: 六通 and 六件 readings are correct; physical sheet/book/cup distractors fail for the intended electronic-message sense. However, the exact email entry explicitly allows conversational つ/個, which the visible neutral question does not exclude. Stored-email 六本 naturalness has weaker support than sending correspondence 一本 and remains qualified.

itemInventory.question: 二枚で一組の申込書に記入して、一{}提出しました。
itemInventory.englishAssessment: The English adds submitting one complete two-sheet form. Japanese establishes the form's composition, but not that both sheets were submitted.
itemInventory.assessment: Document, copy, set, and application-entry units are coherent for a complete submission, with correct listed readings. 頭 and 杯 fail. But filling in a two-sheet form and submitting one sheet is possible, for example when another sheet is retained; no Japanese-side requirement rules that out.

The actual letter-in-envelope label, not an invisible three-sheet sentence, is enough for 通. Pen, car, and cat do not ordinarily take 通 in these noun senses. The source reading is つう, not とおり. No independent reverse note is authored.

itemInventory.rubricQualification: The ambiguity component is provisional for U2: the potential rejected はちつう has not been established as an ordinary exact reading.
itemInventory.cue: Eight complete letters were sent. Write the count using 通, not a sheet count.
itemInventory.assessment: The authored はっつう is directly supported. Exact-reading acceptance completeness remains unresolved rather than being deduced from a short source row. The count-versus-sheets explanation is otherwise accurate.

itemInventory.cue: Ten email messages arrived. Write the count using 通.
itemInventory.assessment: Both exact ten readings are supported. Paragraphs and attachments do not multiply the number of messages; explanation fits the cue.

itemInventory.cue: Eleven complete letters arrived. Write the count using 通.
itemInventory.assessment: The regular compound preserves the verified 一通 reading. The last explanation sentence about envelopes' paper sheets is awkward but not an established substantive defect; see O2.

itemInventory.cue: Ask how many complete application documents are needed. Write only the question quantity using 何 and 通.
itemInventory.assessment: Correct whole quantity and reading. 通つう is distinguished from way-counting 通りとおり; the displayed spelling is not silently replaced.

findings.title: Accepted 六匹 lacks the supported ろくひき typed alternative
findings.evidence: Both cards accept 匹/六匹 and ろっぴき. IMABI's actual ～匹 table, number 6, lists preferred ロッピキ and alternative ロクヒキ. Neither card's good/kana list can normalize ろくひき into the listed kana; there is no hard branch containing it.
findings.learnerImpact: A learner choosing an explicitly permitted animal counter can receive rejection for its documented whole numeric reading.
findings.remedy: Add ろくひき to the v1 kana alternatives of both cards. Keep canonical Read restricted to 六頭ろくとう and 六羽ろくわ/ろっぱ respectively; do not add a different unit's reading to either readingAnswers list.
findings.qualification: This relies on a positive exact-number source entry, not on analogy or on another table's omission. The two sources do not establish equal frequency, and the less common form need not replace the canonical teaching model.

findings.title: Neutral unread-email question rejects ordinary つ and 個 counts
findings.evidence: The full question is まだ読んでいないメールが六{}あります。, with no formal-register or specified-unit restriction. The retrieved メール entry explicitly says conversational counts also use つ and 個. The authored lists allow 通/件/本 but neither つ/六つ/むっつ nor 個/六個/ろっこ.
findings.learnerImpact: Ordinary message counts are rejected despite matching both the visible quantity and the question's neutral register.
findings.remedy: Accept the fitting generic six-count forms in suffix typing, with 六つ read むっつ and 六個 read ろっこ; explain that 通 is the target-specific message counter. Do not treat a conversational alternative as impossible merely because it is not the preferred model. Keep canonical 六通 Read as ろくつう.
findings.qualification: The source distinguishes messages, transmission events, and matters. This finding does not recommend 回 for the existing-message count.

findings.title: Document composition does not say all sheets must be copied or submitted
findings.evidence: 三枚一組の資料 describes the source handout, but 一枚コピーしてください can request copying one sheet from it. Likewise, filling in a 二枚で一組の申込書 does not entail submitting both sheets: 一枚提出しました describes submitting one sheet, potentially retaining the other. The English explicitly adds complete-copy/complete-application intent, and the notes announce it only after the answer. 枚 is an ordinary sheet counter according to the retrieved ～枚 entry.
findings.learnerImpact: A plausible completed Japanese sentence appears among the wrong choices. Learners are asked to infer a whole-set requirement unavailable before answering, so these questions do not securely test the claimed sheet-versus-complete-document distinction.
findings.remedy: Put the complete-set condition on the Japanese question side, explicitly requiring all three pages to be copied together and both application pages to be submitted together. For example, state 三枚とも必要です or 二枚ともそろえて提出しました with a coherent complete-copy count. Alternatively accept the sheet interpretation and stop claiming that the current task exclusively tests complete-set selection. Keep the third 通 forward rather than deleting it, because its reverse owner still requires three.
findings.qualification: The intended 部 and 通 answers are natural and the units themselves are correct. This is an underdetermined learner-visible operation, not a claim that every imaginable part-reading must be accepted in every counter exercise.

locations.claim: 丸ごとのローストチキンを一匹注文しました as an ordinary accepted restaurant-order count
まだ読んでいないメールが六本あります as an ordinary stored-email count

unverifiedClaims.evidence: The inspected 羽 article directly supports a whole bird as meat with 羽. The bird entry supports generic live-animal 匹 but does not attest cooked roast chicken with 匹. The 手紙 entry supports communication 本 with 手紙1本よこさない, while the actual メール entry documents 通/件 and conversational つ/個, not this six-unread-messages 本 collocation. These are evidence limits, not proofs that the alternatives are wrong.
unverifiedClaims.learnerImpact: An accepted-answer list also teaches usage. General counter membership alone is not enough to present every state/register/collocation as an ordinary model.
unverifiedClaims.remedy: Corroborate these exact uses or a closely matching contemporary teaching/dictionary example. If evidence only supports a marked usage, qualify that usage instead of calling it generally ordinary; if it is unsupported or inappropriate, revise the accepted alternative. Do not remove it solely because a short source omits it.
unverifiedClaims.confidence: high that the retrieved evidence does not settle these precise collocations; low-to-medium on whether either usage is actually defective

unverifiedClaims.title: Eight 通: exclusivity of はっつう not established
unverifiedClaims.evidence: IMABI explicitly supplies 八通ハッツウ, which verifies the authored answer. Tofugu's general eight-before-t table allows contracted and uncontracted stems, making はちつう a candidate worth resolving, but a general pattern does not independently verify every exact counter. The direct-source checks did not retrieve a reliable entry settling 八通はちつう. Search-page responses were unusable or irrelevant.
unverifiedClaims.learnerImpact: If はちつう is ordinary, the exclusive Read list produces a false rejection. If it is not ordinary, adding it by analogy would teach an unsupported variant.
unverifiedClaims.remedy: Resolve the exact 八通 variant against a pronunciation dictionary or a precise teaching entry before declaring the exclusive answer set clean. Retain the verified はっつう default; do not automatically add or categorically condemn はちつう on this review's evidence.
unverifiedClaims.confidence: high in はっつう; unresolved in the ordinary status of はちつう
unverifiedClaims.articleQualification: The article's 八通（はっつう） example does not itself claim exclusivity, so this unresolved grading question is not an established article error.
